extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of political philosophy; legislators, jurists, and theorists of government
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting and applying normative criteria about legitimate governmental powers (prerogative, parental, political, despotical) and the moral-legal effects of conquest from a classical political‑philosophy treatise. Focuses on what makes executive acts, laws, and conquests legitimate or illegitimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of prerogative
rubrics_metrics.description: This power to act according to discretion, for the public good, without the prescription of the law, and sometimes even against it, is that which is called prerogative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prerogative exists because lawmakers cannot foresee every emergency or necessity; it is a latitude left to the executive to do things of choice which the laws do not prescribe. It is properly the executive acting for the public good where municipal law gives no direction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legitimacy test for prerogative: public good
rubrics_metrics.description: This power, whilst employed for the benefit of the community, and suitably to the trust and ends of the government, is undoubted prerogative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether an act claimed as prerogative is legitimate is decided by its tendency to the good or hurt of the people. Acts manifestly for the good of the people and establishing government on its true foundations justify themselves; acts that tend to injure or oppress the people are illegitimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted scope of prerogative: cases law cannot foresee
rubrics_metrics.description: Many things there are, which the law can by no means provide for; and those must necessarily be left to the discretion of him that has the executive power in his hands, to be ordered by him as the public good and advantage shall require.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prerogative covers emergencies and unforeseen accidents (e.g., mitigating severity of law, pardoning offenders, actions necessary to preserve members of society) where rigid application of law would do harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerogative must preserve members of society
rubrics_metrics.description: That as much as may be, all the members of the society are to be preserved: for since many accidents may happen, wherein a strict and rigid observation of the laws may do harm... ’tis fit the ruler should have a power, in many cases, to mitigate the severity of the law, and pardon some offenders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fundamental constraint: prerogative is justified only insofar as it furthers preservation of the people; even the guilty are to be spared where it causes no prejudice to the innocent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on prerogative: not to set up private interest
rubrics_metrics.description: A weak and ill prince, who would claim that power ... to make or promote an interest distinct from that of the public, gives the people an occasion to claim their right, and limit that power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prerogative becomes objectionable when used to create or advance a ruler’s private interest or to set up one part or party to the oppression of others; such tendencies justify lawful limitation by the people.

rubrics_metrics.name: On enlarging or defining prerogative by law
rubrics_metrics.description: They have a very wrong notion of government, who say, that the people have encroached upon the prerogative, when they have got any part of it to be defined by positive laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positive laws that limit previously indefinite prerogative are not an encroachment but a clarification to prevent misuse; people may lawfully define prerogative to protect the public good.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive discretion over parliamentary convening must serve public good
rubrics_metrics.description: The power of calling parliaments in England, as to precise time, place, and duration, is certainly a prerogative of the king, but still with this trust, that it shall be made use of for the good of the nation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choices about time, place and duration of assemblies rest with the executive only insofar as they align with exigencies and public interest; such discretionary choices are part of prerogative but constrained by public good.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ultimate remedy when no earthly judge exists
rubrics_metrics.description: Between an executive power in being, with such a prerogative, and a legislative that depends upon his will for their convening, there can be no judge on earth... The people have no other remedy in this... but to appeal to heaven.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When rulers exercise power without right and no earthly check exists, the people retain an antecedent, paramount right (appeal to heaven) to judge whether they have cause to resist; this is an ultimate constraint, not a license for disorder except where necessity and majority justify it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and limits of paternal power
rubrics_metrics.description: Paternal or parental power is nothing but that which parents have over their children, to govern them for the children’s good, till they come to the use of reason... the paternal is a natural government, but not at all extending itself to the ends and jurisdictions of that which is political.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paternal power exists during minority for instruction, help and preservation; it does not extend to life and death, nor to perpetual subjection once the child reaches reason; it does not reach the child's property which is for the child's disposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and limits of political power
rubrics_metrics.description: Political power is that power, which every man having in the state of nature, has given up into the hands of the society... to be employed for their good, and the preservation of their property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Political power originates in compact/consent and is limited to means necessary to preserve lives, liberties, and possessions. It is not absolute; penalties and laws may be annexed only so far as they tend to preservation of the whole society.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of despotical power (when it arises)
rubrics_metrics.description: Despotical power is an absolute, arbitrary power one man has over another, to take away his life, whenever he pleases. This... is the effect only of forfeiture, which the aggressor makes of his own life, when he puts himself into the state of war with another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Despotical power is not conferred by nature or compact but arises from forfeiture in the state of war; captives taken in a just and lawful war are subject to such power, and it cannot be lawfully created by agreement with someone who retains mastery of his own life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Origination triad: paternal, political, despotical
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature gives the first of these, viz. paternal power... Voluntary agreement gives the second, viz. political power... And forfeiture gives the third despotical power to lords for their own benefit, over those who are stripped of all property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear differentiation of sources: natural relation for parents; consent/compact for civil government; forfeiture (just cause/state of war) for despotical rule. This determines legitimacy and scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absolute dominion inconsistent with civil society
rubrics_metrics.description: Absolute dominion, however placed, is so far from being one kind of civil society, that it is as inconsistent with it, as slavery is with property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Political authority grounded in compact cannot legitimately be absolute; the nature and ends of civil society (preservation of persons and property) forbid absolute arbitrary rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conquest does not of itself create legitimate government
rubrics_metrics.description: Conquest is as far from setting up any government, as demolishing an house is from building a new one in the place... without the consent of the people, can never erect a new one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Force alone (unjust conquest) cannot found a rightful political authority over the conquered; legitimacy requires the consent of the people. Extorted promises or submissions obtained by force do not constitute true consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights of conqueror are limited: life and reparation, not blanket title
rubrics_metrics.description: The right then of conquest extends only to the lives of those who joined in the war, not to their estates, but only in order to make reparation for the damages received, and the charges of the war... The conqueror has a title to reparation for damages received, and the children have a title to their father’s estate for their subsistence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A lawful conqueror may have despotical power over those who engaged in unjust force (up to life) and a claim to reparation for damages, but he does not thereby acquire rightful dominion over the possessions or posterity of the conquered. Property rights of innocents (wives, children, noncombatants) are preserved; satisfy the more pressing claims first (preservation of children) if resources are insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extorted promises and coerced transfers bind not
rubrics_metrics.description: Promises extorted by force, without right, can be thought consent... They bind not at all; because whatsoever another gets from me by force, I still retain the right of, and he is obliged presently to restore.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracts, conveyances or promises obtained under coercion are invalid: extorted obligations do not transfer rightful title and the injured party retains right of restitution or self-rescue when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conquered peoples retain right to reconstitute government
rubrics_metrics.description: Over those then that joined with him in the war, and over those of the subdued country that opposed him not, and the posterity even of those that did, the conqueror, even in a just war, hath, by his conquest, no right of dominion: they are free from any subjection to him, and if their former government be dissolved, they are at liberty to begin and erect another to themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when force compels submission, absent valid consent the people retain the natural right to reconstitute a government that secures their approval and preservation; conquest does not extinguish this liberty.
